sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the word that completes 'bound in ___'. The baker hasn't seen that wording and can't work it out. Card 11 also says 'kingdom of heaven' just before it, which points to the answer.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: Verse 25 gets no story card before it. The blank asks the baker to guess the wording 'will ___ it', and 'keep' and 'guard' read as natural as 'lose'. A thoughtful baker has no way to reason to the answer.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

sonnet.problem: Card 15 already says 'the Son of Man will come in His Father's glory'. The right answer, 'The Son of Man coming in His kingdom', echoes that line and the 'Son of Man' in card 1, while the wrong answers share none of it. The right answer gives itself away and stands out.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The card calls back to Jesus calling Peter blessed (Matthew 16:17) but cites only 16:22.
sonnet.rule: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

sonnet.problem: John the Baptist shows up for the first time with no short label saying who he is.
sonnet.rule: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
